title: What do an x402 facilitator's verify and settle steps do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced guide to the x402 facilitator interface: the read-only verify call, the committing settle call, the response fields and the XRPL payment flow around them.
body:
According to the X402 version 2 specification, a facilitator is a service that handles payment verification and blockchain settlement, offered through HTTP endpoints that a resource server can delegate to a trusted third party or host itself. [1]

POST /verify checks a payment authorization without executing it on the blockchain: it is read-only, must not commit payment state or write onchain state, and returns isValid, an invalidReason when the payment is invalid, and the payer. POST /settle durably commits the payment and returns success, the transaction hash (an empty string if none was broadcast), the network in CAIP-2 format and the payer. GET /supported lists the payment schemes, networks and extensions the facilitator handles. [1]

According to the x402 exact-scheme specification for XRPL, the client signs a Payment transaction and sends it in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. The resource server calls /verify, and the facilitator decodes the signed transaction and checks it against the requirements, including transaction type, destination, network and amount. On success the server calls /settle, the facilitator re-runs verification and submits the transaction to the XRPL network named in the requirements, and once settlement is validated the server grants access with a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header. The older names X-PAYMENT and X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE are deprecated. [2]

Author interpretation: a successful verify is not a payment. An agent should treat a resource as paid only when settlement reports success with a transaction hash that appears in a validated ledger. In this scheme the payer, not the facilitator, pays the XRPL network fee. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1][2]
